item.title: Milo Yiannopoulos deported after U.S. immigration arrest, officials say
item.description: Milo Yiannopoulos, who is British, was accused of overstaying his visa after entering the country legally in May 2019.

item.title: Nepal flash flood deaths surpass 600, with around 3,000 still missing
item.description: A Nepali Army spokesperson said early Saturday that helicopter operations were on hold until weather conditions improved.

item.title: Californios brings a Michelin-starred Mexican menu to San Francisco
item.description: Val and Carolyn Cantú reimagine Mexican cuisine at San Francisco restaurant Californios, which has earned three Michelin stars for its 12-course tasting menu.

item.title: Pierre Laborde makes New York City's next "it bag" in his Harlem workshop
item.description: Haitian-born designer Pierre Laborde can't make his popular bags fast enough to keep up with intense demand. Eager shoppers queue outside of a weekly market in New York City to try to buy one of his bags.

item.title: How long will the Lindsay Clancy trial jury take to reach a verdict?
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial jury​ will resume their deliberations Monday. It could be days before they reach a verdict, a legal expert says.

item.title: Iran vows to resist U.S. sanctions as war passes 6-month mark
item.description: As the war passes the six-month mark, neither side showed any sign of backing down.

item.title: Parents call Dolly Parton's book charity for children "a gift"
item.description: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library charity has brought books to thousands of small hands eager to read. Parents of children who were gifted books through the charity praise the late singer, emphasizing their gratefulness.

item.title: Cozy up with this fall's most anticipated books
item.description: Amazon Books editorial director Sarah Gelman discusses some of the most hotly anticipated books of the fall.

item.title: What is rejection sensitive dysphoria? A doctor explains
item.description: ADHD expert and psychiatrist Dr. Sasha Hamdani explains the science behind rejection sensitive dysphoria (RSD) and explores its connection to ADHD in her new book, "Too Sensitive: Rejection, Resilience, and the Science of Feeling Deeply."

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Desperate search for survivors in Nepal amid fears of a second flood
item.description: Flash flooding crashed through the border of Nepal and Tibet after a Himalayan glacier collapsed, killing more than 600 people. Rescue crews race against time to find any survivors out of the estimated 2,500 people believed to be missing.

item.title: Dolly Parton "loved being called the book lady," charity president remembers
item.description: Tonight, Nashville's Grand Ole Opry will remember Dolly Parton in a star-studded tribute. The beloved country singer was also celebrated for her humanitarian efforts, including her Imagination Library charity, which promoted literacy for young readers. The Dollywood Foundation president Jeff Conyers joined "CBS Saturday Morning" to speak on Dolly's generous soul.

item.title: Nashville airport could be renamed for Dolly Parton under new proposal
item.description: The international airport in Nashville, Tennessee, would be renamed for Dolly Parton under a proposal by Tennessee's governor.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 30): "By Design"
item.description: "Sunday Morning" presents its annual edition touching on all aspects of design, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Meta settles social media addiction suit for up to $17.1 billion
item.description: Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion to settle allegations that its social media platforms are addictive.

item.title: What Meta's massive $17 billion social media addiction settlement means for your family
item.description: Tech giant Meta settled a series of multistate social media addiction lawsuits, agreeing to pay out up to $17 billion. In addition, Meta will roll out some changes to its portfolio of social media apps, including Instagram, Facebook and others.

item.title: Inflation still high as Iran war hits 6 months and Trump's tariffs continue
item.description: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh says the central bank may be forced to act if inflation does not cool. This comes as President Trump's war in Iran crosses the six month mark and his tariff tiff with Canada contributes to higher prices on either side of the border.

item.title: Video shows Philly officer leaving person in street before deadly hit-and-run
item.description: Philadelphia police are investigating an officer who failed to help a person in the street who was killed in a hit-and-run in Olney.

item.title: ICE deports Venezuelan father from Texas to West Africa
item.description: Carlos Tellez Sanchez had worked at a car dealership in Dallas during the day and drove for Uber Eats at night to support his family.

item.title: 8/29: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: Rescue efforts in Nepal, high inflation six months after the Iran war started, plus Dolly Parton's Imagination Library brings books to young readers.

item.title: U.S. takes out refueling station for alleged drug-trafficking boats
item.description: The vessel, which was in international waters near Ecuador, was allegedly used as a floating refueling station for drug boats belonging to the Los Choneros organization.

item.title: Russian strike on Ukrainian warehouse kills 37, one of deadliest attacks of 2026
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy suggested warehouse near a residential area hit by a Russian strike was used to store ammunition.

item.title: Man with sinus infection symptoms diagnosed with heart condition
item.description: Marc Gaudisosi thought his symptoms were caused by a sinus infection. Then an urgent care told him to go to the hospital.

item.description: A California couple were in a Nepali village when an avalanche of powerful waters ripped down from the high Himalayas toward them.
